title: Introduce queued request trimmer and safety halo to mitigate intermittent region panics
author: Marcus Chen
body: Summary: This PR adds a lightweight queued-request trimmer and a region-level safety-halo to reduce tail-latency amplification during short-lived regional overloads that were causing intermittent region panics and SLO violations. Motivation: During a Feb incident we observed a cascade where large in-flight queues plus heavy KV cache pressure pushed a region into degraded state, triggering aggressive circuit transitions and long recoveries. The root cause is combination of unbounded per-connection queued requests and a lack of a soft backoff mechanism that temporarily trims low-priority queued work while preserving critical SLO-bearing requests. Goals: 1) prevent self-amplifying latency spikes by trimming old queued requests under pressure, 2) provide a temporary safety-halo that soft-marks a region as "safeguarded" so controllers avoid heavy rebalancing for short windows, 3) ship as a hotfix with feature flags and safe rollback. Changes included: - runtime/queue/trimmer.go: new trimmed-queue policy and metrics (TrimOldRequests, TrimThreshold heuristics). - controlplane/safety/halo.go: safety-halo coordinator responsible for ephemeral region state and decay timer. - console/telemetry/alerts.yaml: new alert SLO_TRIMMED_REQUEST_RATE and dashboard panels for halo duration/overlaps. - deploy/k8s/hotfix.yaml: canary rollout config, feature-flag env VAR QUEUE_TRIM_ENABLED and HALO_TTL_MS. - tests/integration/queue_trim_test.go: deterministic unit tests for trimming behavior under synthetic load and randomized ordering. - docs/ops/incident_playbooks/queue-trim.md: short runbook for ops to toggle and interpret halo telemetry. Commit summary: (a) 8f3d1ef add queued request trimmer and trim policy (b) d2b7c54 introduce safety halo coordinator and controllers shim (c) 4a1e6b2 add telemetry panels and alerts (d) b9c7d01 add integration tests and canary k8s manifest Decisions and tradeoffs: - Trimming policy is prioritized: it will only drop non-critical, non-hedged queued requests and never remove requests flagged as SLO-critical or pinned by tenants. This keeps customer-facing latency predictable. - Safety-halo is intentionally short-lived (defaults 30s) to avoid masking longer systemic issues; it prevents large-scale rebalancing for short bursts. - Feature gated behind QUEUE_TRIM_ENABLED and HALO_ENABLED for controlled rollout. Tests and CI: - Unit tests added covering trimming heuristics and state transitions. - Integration test simulating queue spike and verifying that halo prevents circuit storm while trimmed request ratio remains under configured thresholds. - CI initially failed one flaky integration test on first run; flaky test fixed by adding deterministic seed and mock clock; final CI status: pass. Review conversation (condensed): - Priya Shah (reviewer): "Can trimming ever starve retry loops? Please document retry semantics and ensure idempotency." Author reply: "Trim only affects queued, not in-flight, retries; updated docs and added tests to assert retry behavior." - Ethan Morgan: "Are halo TTLs observable per-region?" Author: "Yes, telemetry exposes halo_start, halo_end, and reason labels; added dashboard panels." - Sofia Alvarez: "How does this interact with Dedicated autoscaler?" Author: "Halo sets a temporary scale-suspend flag observed by autoscaler; autoscaler respects suspend for TTL with a safety-boundary override." - Security review (automated): no secrets or high-privilege changes. Rollout plan and rollback: - Canary rollout to 10% of regions for 24h with automated telemetry checks: trimmed_request_rate < 2% and no SLO regressions in 5m windows. - If trimmed_request_rate > 5% or error rate increases, the operator can toggle QUEUE_TRIM_ENABLED=0 and HALO_ENABLED=0; a documented rollback command is included in the runbook. Telemetry and alerting: - New metrics: rqueue_trimmed_count, rqueue_trimmed_rate, region_halo_active, region_halo_reason - New alert: SLO_TRIMMED_REQUEST_RATE fires if trimmed rate > 5% sustained for 10m during canary. Backout and long-term work: - This is a hotfix to stop cascade behavior; long-term we plan to: 1) integrate request-prioritization at ingress, 2) extend proactive KV pressure signals to the router for earlier diffusing of pressure, 3) evaluate adaptive TTL for halo based on observed tail-latency. Release notes: This patch reduces the risk of short-lived region panics by trimming low-priority queued requests and introducing a short safety-halo to avoid cascade rebalances. Ops can toggle via QUEUE_TRIM_ENABLED/HALO_ENABLED. Merge outcome: merged to main via squash on 2026-02-28 after approvals from Priya, Ethan, and Sofia. Linear links: ENG-8472 SRE-1593. CI: final status pass. Files changed: runtime/queue/trimmer.go controlplane/safety/halo.go console/telemetry/alerts.yaml deploy/k8s/hotfix.yaml tests/integration/queue_trim_test.go docs/ops/incident_playbooks/queue-trim.md.

release_notes: Hotfix: Trim low-priority queued requests and add ephemeral region safety halo to reduce cascade panics and SLO regressions. Feature-gated; ops toggles documented.
notes_for_ops: Monitor rqueue_trimmed_rate and region_halo_active. Canary to 10% regions for 24h. Rollback: set QUEUE_TRIM_ENABLED=0 HALO_ENABLED=0 in canary manifest.
changelog_entry: Fix: reduce region panic cascade by trimming queued non-critical requests and adding short safety halo (QUEUETRIM+HALO feature flags).
risk_assessment: low-medium: changes are feature gated with canary rollout and observable metrics; trimming never removes SLO-critical requests and safety-halo is time-limited.
